purpose: Prevent premature CISA outreach while continuously watching for a reproducible foreign technical event with a concrete U.S. communications-resilience nexus.
gate_law: CISA opens on technical evidence, not on censorship prevalence, propaganda content, vendor nationality, or geopolitical suspicion.

required_dimensions.TECHNICAL_REPRODUCIBILITY: At least two independent foreign vantage points or networks reproduce a path/protocol-specific effect.
required_dimensions.NEGATIVE_CONTROL: The destination service is healthy from unaffected networks and/or provider-side status confirms no provider-local outage.
required_dimensions.PATH_OR_POLICY_LOCALIZATION: Traceroute, ASN, DNS, TLS, QUIC, reset/drop, routing, or allowlist evidence localizes the event to a foreign network/control segment.
required_dimensions.US_NEXUS: The event materially affects access to U.S.-hosted/U.S.-operated communications, cloud, software, financial, media, diplomatic, humanitarian, commercial, or partner-critical services.
required_dimensions.ATTRIBUTION_DISCIPLINE: Any claim of Russian/TSPU involvement requires device, operator, vendor-control-channel, configuration, or other direct control-plane evidence.

opens_gate_if: A stable basket of U.S./open services becomes unreachable or sharply degraded from multiple foreign networks.
Local/approved services on those same networks remain normally reachable.
Matched external controls show the U.S. services themselves are healthy.
TLS/QUIC/DNS/HTTP interference is reproducible and localized to the same foreign AS, border segment, middlebox, or operator domain.
The behavior differs on a matched alternate route or network.
Packet/protocol behavior is specific enough to distinguish policy interference from generic congestion or outage.
Two or more countries or independent foreign operator groups enter a materially similar deny/allowlist state within a narrow time window.
The same U.S./open-service basket is disproportionately affected.
Independent technical evidence shows a shared vendor/control/configuration or other bridge beyond timing alone.

Public or lawfully obtained evidence identifies remote-management/control channels, shared orchestrator infrastructure, synchronized configuration delivery, or direct operator/vendor linkage across borders.
The bridge temporally precedes or coincides with the observed network policy change.
Foreign traffic unexpectedly shifts through a new transit jurisdiction/AS or route origin and the shift coincides with selective service loss.
Matched bypass paths restore reachability or remove the censorship fingerprint.
RPKI/BGP history supports the path-change interpretation.
A frozen technical event is followed by a measurable source-substitution or information-manipulation burst.
The technical event is independently sufficient to satisfy T1, T2, T3, T4 or T5.
The information layer is treated as impact/context, not as proof of the network actor.

fresh_global_calibration.finding: Internet shutdown followed by selective social-media blocking and service whitelisting.
fresh_global_calibration.reason: No U.S.-specific impact, multi-country synchronization, or shared external control-plane bridge established.

fresh_global_calibration.finding: OONI measured TLS interference with RST injection after ClientHello on one tested mobile network while other websites remained accessible.
fresh_global_calibration.reason: Useful protocol baseline but no U.S.-resilience nexus or cross-border control bridge.

fresh_global_calibration.finding: Both countries began blocking Discord on the same day, while OONI documented Türkiye-specific censorship fingerprints.
fresh_global_calibration.reason: Temporal coincidence alone has zero attribution weight.

fresh_global_calibration.finding: Live SS7/Diameter surveillance attack telemetry was mapped to operator signalling infrastructure across multiple jurisdictions.
fresh_global_calibration.reason: Demonstrates that foreign telecom interconnect can create transnational technical exposure, but it is surveillance signaling abuse rather than a TSPU-like public-internet denial event.

decision_logic.GREEN_HOLD: Background censorship/shutdown/DPI evidence only; collect and calibrate.
decision_logic.YELLOW_INTENSIFY: One strong technical trigger dimension or multiple weak independent signals; freeze baseline and increase OONI/RIPE/BGP measurements.
decision_logic.ORANGE_PREPARE_CISA: At least two independent technical trigger classes, including T1/T2/T3/T4/T5, plus a clear U.S. nexus; preserve evidence and prepare submission.
decision_logic.RED_SEND_CISA: Reproducible foreign path/policy interference with negative controls, U.S. service/communications impact, and at least one cross-border or control-plane bridge. Attribution can remain UNKNOWN if the resilience event itself is real.

anti_false_positive_rules: Domestic censorship alone never opens CISA.
Single-country shutdown alone never opens CISA.
Shared vendor alone never opens CISA.
Russian-origin SORM equipment alone never opens CISA.
Same-day blocking in two countries alone never opens CISA.
FIMI/social-media activity alone never opens CISA.
Provider-side outage or cloud RCA closes the external-network hypothesis unless independent residual evidence remains.
VPN success is a useful clue but not sufficient attribution because route, resolver, protocol and egress all change simultaneously.
measurement_stack: RIPE Atlas DNS, ping and traceroute
RIPE RIS / RouteViews / BGPStream route history
provider status and public RCA negative controls
lawful packet captures from consenting controlled endpoints
independent replication from different ASNs and countries
